Market stance

Prof's overnight bullish divergence — S&P new lows with a VIX lower high and futures ramping into a possible short squeeze — meets iain's discipline (short former leaders on bounces, never current leaders) and Enrich's rotation out of NVDA into AVGO and AMD.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • Anthropic IPO pricing reported this week — Venu flags it as a possible SPCX catalyst
  • Prof's short-squeeze watch — futures ramping hard overnight; “one of the most waited short squeeze”
  • NVDA rotation — Enrich is rotating out of NVDA into AVGO and AMD; NVDA fell 2.89% to a new 52-week low
  • QQQ's 647 — a third test decides the double bottom; 696 is the high to beat

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Wednesday split the group between a possible turn and a market to short. The headline is the 200-day: SPY closed below its own 200-day SMA for the first time — 730.20 against 732.55, 0.32% under it (yesterday it sat 0.01% above) — while QQQ bounced +0.39% to 659.51 and held above Remz's 647. Prof's overnight read is the counterweight: the S&P made new lows but the VIX made a lower high (24.55, −3.54% at close, vs the ~28.5 spike) — “a potential bullish divergence, suggesting fear isn't accelerating with the selling” — and the Nasdaq refused new lows, with E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures at 27,558.75, +1.37% on the day. Futures kept ramping after the close (US 500 7,373.1, +0.68%; US Tech 100 27,482.1, +1.35% at ~18:59) and Prof calls it “one of the most waited short squeeze”. Remz's QQQ chart is the level that decides it: top 763 in early October, lower highs 726 then 696, the flush 684 to 647 in one day, and 647 now tested twice — “647 is a MUST hold… Closes under 647 and the double bottom is gone.” iain draws the other line: don't short current leaders near 52-week highs — short former leaders (MRVL, ARM, INTC) showing distribution and broken weekly structure, on bounces into declining 9/21 EMAs with tight risk. Enrich is the rotation: out of NVDA into AVGO and AMD — AVGO held for 100–150%+, reclaimed its 50-week EMA, trigger is to hold today's high 357.34 then break the prior-month high 380.84 on volume; AMD held up too, +5.31% to 530.14, which closes above Remz's 526 short invalidation from yesterday. His RIOT thesis adds a brewing setup: OI off the charts, two-week relative strength, volume, a major trend-line bounce, flagging on the daily, Top 5 on LeadR — “something is brewing”. Remz also opens an ABBV short (rejected at 303, trigger under 289.70 hit, targets 282 then 275) and calls XLV “SCARY”. Venu's RS leaders are the long side of the tape: TSLA holding its 200-day SMA (383.72 vs 382.08), SPOT holding its flag, U and APP standouts — though U gave back its 50.06 breakout by the close and APP sits under a falling 30-week MA, so the framework disagrees with Venu on APP. DiCarlo is the caution: NOT buying ASTS, back at the largest-timeframe Smart Money Zone after a −7.61% day to a new low. Sean posts mindset only. Your process gives five genuine long qualifiers with triggers above the close (TSLA, AMZN, AMD, CRWD, SPOT), one live short (ABBV, trigger already hit) and three defined bounce-shorts (MRVL, ARM, INTC) — plus AVGO, RIOT, SPCX, U and APP as contested or pending, where the trader's call meets a chart that has not confirmed it yet. The declines, not entries: NVDA at a new 52-week low, ASTS at a new 52-week low, and MRVL, ARM and INTC still deep in decline. The discipline is in the framing: SPY lost its 200-day and QQQ is under its 50-week EMA too — so the framework says wait for a hold above the triggers, or a pullback into the averages, and QQQ's 647 is the line that decides whether the divergence or the decline wins.

The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. SPY's invalidation 732.55 is its 200-day SMA. QQQ's invalidation 647.05 is its 3-month low and Remz's must-hold level.
